newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-MARTHA'S SON CROWNED CHAMPION TWO-MILER.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-MARTHA'S SON CROWNED CHAMPION TWO-MILER.

text.p: Martha's Son jumped superbly and powered up the Cheltenham Hill in spectacular fashion on Wednesday to be crowned champion two-mile chaser.

The 9-1 shot, ridden by Rodney Farrant and back at his sparkling best after being laid off for 18 months with injury, landed the Queen Mother Champion Chase at the shrine of steeplechasing with a two-and-a-half length victory over the 6-1 chance Ask Tom. Viking Flagship, who was bidding for a third victory in the race, finished third, half a length back.
Veteran trainer Tim Forster, who saw his charge Maamur killed at Cheltenham on Tuesday, said of Martha's Son: "He is the sweetest, kindest, nicest horse I have ever had to deal with.
"A child of five could ride him. You could take him down to Ludlow (Forster's training base), tie him up and go shopping."
Martha's Son won his first nine races over fences but then was sidelined by injury. He returned to racing at Kempton only to fall at the second fence. On Wednesday he was foot perfect.
"No horse had had a more imperfect preparation," Forster said, praising jockey Farrant for what he called a brilliant ride.
Ask Tom led the field at a steady pace just ahead of the hot favourite Strong Promise who put paid to his chances when clouting the third last.
Martha's Son was well placed throughout and produced a faultless round of jumping to run out a gutsy winner.
Viking Flagship could never get an effective challenge and last year's winner Klairon Davis finished a disappointing fourth.
Arctic Kinsman was withdrawn at the start after breaking a blood vessel
Irish supporters had their first chance to celebrate when the 6-5 favourite Istabraq came from last to first to land the Sun Alliance Hurdle.
Istabraq, the 11th festival success for Irish champion jockey Charlie Swann, showed real courage after being bumped badly at the second last.
"I would say it was courage alone that got her through. No other horse would have finished in the first 10," said trainer Aidan O'Brien.
The winning owner, J.P McManus, paid a rich tribute afterwards to John Durkan, who recommended Istabraq to him and is now being treated for leukaemia in a New York hospital.
Durkan was given the good news by mobile telephone from the unsaddling enclosure.
